1.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/NumberInput/NumberInput.js – This is the main React implementation that renders the two caret buttons and wires up their click handlers. To support alternate controls (e.g. different icons, replaced caret buttons, or custom increment/decrement UI), this file’s render method and event‐handling logic must be updated.
2. packages/components/src/components/number-input/number-input.js – This is the vanilla JS/web component version of NumberInput, which also sets up its own up/down icon event delegation. If alternate controls are to be supported in the Web Components implementation, its constructor and _handleClick logic will need adjustment here.
3. packages/react/src/components/NumberInput/NumberInput-story.js – The Storybook story defines knobs and demonstrates the default caret controls. To show off new control options in the docs, this story should be updated to expose and render the alternative control variants.
4. packages/react/src/components/NumberInput/NumberInput-test.js – The unit tests assume two caret buttons (up and down glyphs) and assert on click behavior. When other control options are introduced—new icons or UI—the tests must be updated to cover the new controls and ensure existing functionality continues to pass.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows the Carbon <NumberInput> rendered with a label “Number Input label” above a text input set to “50”, flanked on its right by the default caret-up and caret-down icons. The user’s request is to explore alternative control options instead of (or in addition to) the up/down carets—for example custom icons, button rows, or any other UI affordance to increment/decrement the value.
